_about: Insurance Estate Map model. Built by tools/build_map_data.py --map insurance. State as of 2023 (historical).

header.eyebrow: Finance Technology · State as of 2023, not current · Oracle Fusion Cloud
header.title: Insurance Estate Map
header.lede: Policy administration, payroll, procurement and banking feed one Oracle ledger per entity; a finance data warehouse on ADW and Enterprise EPM sit around it for reporting, planning and close. Select any system to see what it does, how it connects and where to read more.

footer: Source: finance-technology notebook 2020–2023 (anonymised). Shows the state as of 2023, not the current state.

nodes.title: Policy administration
nodes.subtitle: Exceed · premium & claims
nodes.description: The insurance system of record for policies, premium, commission, claims and case reserves.
functions: Issues, renews and cancels policies; bills premium and pays commission
Records claims, losses and case reserves
Reporting data lands in the on-premise BIM database, then in the ADW insurance data mart (premium one day in arrears, reserves two)
Its activity reaches the ledger as daily Premium, Loss and Claims journals

nodes.title: Payroll
nodes.subtitle: ADP
nodes.description: Payroll processing; produces the payroll journal file for the ledger.
functions: Runs payroll per pay period
Produces a GL file with pay codes mapped to Oracle accounts
Target path: SFTP → OIC → GL (legacy: manual upload)

nodes.title: Corporate card
nodes.subtitle: Visa
nodes.description: Corporate card programme feeding employee expenses.
functions: Daily card transaction file
Loaded directly into Oracle Expenses without a decryption server
Card transactions become expense report lines

nodes.title: Investments
nodes.subtitle: Clearwater · planned
nodes.description: Investment accounting for the bond and equity portfolio; journal interface planned at go-live.
functions: Investment accounting and portfolio reporting
Journals to GL planned through OIC
Investment P&L reported separately in Financial Reporting

nodes.title: Oracle HCM
nodes.subtitle: workers · directory
nodes.description: Oracle HCM Cloud: the worker record used by Expenses, approvals and single sign-on.
functions: Holds workers, managers and departments used by approval hierarchies
Integrates with Expenses for employee data
Sends daily change and weekly full worker extracts for directory accounts and single sign-on

nodes.title: On-premise warehouses
nodes.subtitle: EDW · BIM · HDS (SQL Server)
nodes.description: On-premise SQL Server data stores: the enterprise data warehouse (EDW), the BIM reporting database with Exceed policy data, and HDS. None of them is Essbase.
functions: EDW: enterprise data warehouse with a Finance workgroup database
BIM: policy, premium and claims reporting data from Exceed; source of legacy BIM reports
HDS: data store; some BIM reports sourced from DB2 through it
A load server copies BIM data into the ADW insurance data mart

nodes.title: Oracle Integration Cloud
nodes.subtitle: orchestrations · REST · SOAP
nodes.description: The integration platform for scheduled and event-driven flows into and out of Fusion.
functions: Invokes BI Publisher reports and loads the output into ADW tables
Runs the ERP bulk-extract pattern (ESS job, business event, download)
Updates suppliers through REST (business classifications)
Carries payroll and planned investment journals into GL

nodes.title: OneCloud
nodes.subtitle: scheduler · data mover
nodes.description: Third-party cloud scheduler and data-integration tool around EPM, OAC and ADW.
functions: Loads Planning financials into the OAC Essbase reporting cube
Moves Payables imaging audit data into ADW
Copies EPM and Essbase backups on-premise
Back-load chain reruns a missed policy journal load

nodes.title: EPM Data Management
nodes.subtitle: GL ↔ EPM
nodes.description: EPM's integration layer between the Fusion ledger and the EPM applications.
functions: Loads GL actuals into Planning (and the close application)
Exports budget and statistical journals back to GL budget balances
Maps Fusion COA members to EPM dimensions

nodes.title: File loaders
nodes.subtitle: FBDI · spreadsheets · REST
nodes.description: Standard Oracle bulk loaders used for journals, conversions and master data.
functions: Journal import for the daily policy journals after Financial Integrator mapping
Spreadsheet loaders for journals, budgets and segment values / hierarchies
Go-live conversions: 5 years of GL balances, suppliers, assets, open POs, contracts

nodes.title: Suppliers
nodes.subtitle: registration · qualification
nodes.description: The supplier master with registration, qualification and enrichment.
functions: Supplier registration with approval for prospective and internal suppliers
Qualification questionnaires score business classifications (diversity)
DataFox enriches supplier firmographics
An OIC interface updates business classifications through REST
An APEX app maintains qualification questions through REST

nodes.title: Procurement & contracts
nodes.subtitle: requisitions · agreements
nodes.description: Self-Service Procurement, purchasing agreements and supplier contracts.
functions: Requisitions approved by amount tier (to 5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, over 250K)
Blanket and contract purchase agreements; agreement change orders can auto-approve
Supplier contracts (MSA, CSA, SOW, NDA) with signed PDFs in Enterprise Contracts
Home-page tile for contracts expiring this week

nodes.title: Purchasing & receipts
nodes.subtitle: POs · accruals
nodes.description: Purchase orders and receipts; uninvoiced receipts accrue at period end.
functions: Purchase orders from requisitions and agreements
Receipts against POs (three-way match)
Period-end chain: transfer to costing, then Create Uninvoiced Receipt Accruals
Only received-over-invoiced amounts accrue; finally closed POs drop off the accrual report

nodes.title: Payables & imaging
nodes.subtitle: invoices · approvals
nodes.description: Supplier invoices captured by email and OCR, matched, and approved by amount tier.
functions: Integrated Invoice Imaging: email in, OCR, import to Payables
Invoice approval by tier; over 250K to an approval group; PO-matched and recurring invoices auto-approve
Credit memo and one-time payment rules
Imaging audit data goes to ADW for a dashboard

nodes.title: Payments & cash
nodes.subtitle: Bank A · BAI2
nodes.description: Payment runs, bank files and bank statement reconciliation.
functions: Payment process requests with payment approval by approval group
ACH and control-totals file, and Positive Pay for printed checks, to Bank A over SFTP
BAI2 bank statements reconciled in Cash Management (new with Fusion)

nodes.title: Expenses
nodes.subtitle: card · out of pocket
nodes.description: Employee expense reports, fed by the corporate card and HCM.
functions: Corporate card transactions loaded daily
Expense approval with an override-approver privilege
Approved reports become Payables invoices

nodes.title: Fixed Assets
nodes.subtitle: assets
nodes.description: Asset subledger fed from Payables.
functions: Additions from Payables
Depreciation by book
Closed on business day 3–4

nodes.title: Intercompany & allocations
nodes.subtitle: Mutual ↔ Agency
nodes.description: Intercompany billing between the Mutual and the Agency, and allocation rules.
functions: Monthly shared-services billing from the Mutual to the Agency through Oracle Intercompany
Receiving organisation approves; batches transfer to GL; settlement clears receivable and payable
Allocation rule sets (source, target, range, basis, offset) post to allocation companies 81–89

nodes.title: Subledger Accounting
nodes.subtitle: rules engine
nodes.description: One accounting engine for Payables, Purchasing receipts, Payments and Assets.
functions: Journal entry rule sets, account rules and mapping sets per subledger
Creates accounting for accruals, invoices, payments and assets
Transfers to GL by category

nodes.title: General Ledger
nodes.subtitle: Mutual · Agency · 8-segment COA
nodes.description: The ledgers for the Mutual and the Agency, on one 8-segment chart of accounts.
functions: Company, Department, Account, Product, State, Class, Project, Intercompany
Hierarchies published to the GL balances cube for FRS, Smart View and OTBI
Journal approval by group; auto-reverse by category to the next period
Closed on business day 6; statutory balance sheet shows surplus
Segment value security and cross-validation rules

nodes.title: Enterprise EPM
nodes.subtitle: close · planning · reconciliation
nodes.description: Oracle Enterprise EPM: close task manager, planning, narrative reporting, reconciliation, tax reporting.
functions: Close task manager with calendar, owners and sign-off
Planning for budgets and forecasts; budgets go back to GL
Narrative Reporting packages with author, review and sign-off phases
Account Reconciliation since September 2021
Migrated to the Enterprise EPM bundle in 2022

nodes.title: Autonomous Data Warehouse
nodes.subtitle: Oracle Autonomous Database
nodes.description: Oracle Autonomous Database (Data Warehouse workload): the Finance Transaction Data Warehouse, holding transaction-level data from Fusion, PeopleSoft history and policy data. Not Essbase.
functions: Financial report mart of all Fusion transactional modules (live February 2021)
PeopleSoft Financials history
Insurance data mart (stage, temp, integrated-journal schemas) fed from BIM for premium, claims and policy counts
Loaded from Fusion through OIC (BI Publisher reports, bulk extracts) and OneCloud
SQL checks reconcile daily policy journals and extracts to source; source for OAC dashboards and BI Publisher

nodes.title: Oracle Analytics Cloud
nodes.subtitle: BI · Essbase · DV
nodes.description: Oracle Analytics Cloud: dashboards, the Essbase financials cube and data visualisation.
functions: BI dashboards on a semantic model (physical, logical, presentation layers)
Essbase financials cube loaded from Planning (OneCloud) and ADW metrics; one of two Essbase cubes, with the Fusion GL balances cube
Data Visualization with data flows and data sets (e.g. AP imaging auditability)
Report outputs distributed to a content-cloud folder for Accounting

nodes.title: Fusion reporting
nodes.subtitle: OTBI · BIP · FRS · Smart View
nodes.description: Reporting inside Fusion: real-time analyses, pixel-perfect reports, financial statements and Excel analysis.
functions: OTBI: real-time subject areas for GL balances and journals, P2P, and subledger-to-ledger reconciliation
BI Publisher: custom reports and data models; replaced about 130 legacy reports with about 50
Financial Reporting Studio: about 20 statements, including statutory balance sheet, statement of surplus, P&L by product
Smart View: ad hoc analysis on the GL balances cube
Transactional KPIs: invoices processed and paid on time, PO-backed %, payment method mix

nodes.title: Bank A
nodes.subtitle: ACH · Positive Pay · BAI2
nodes.description: The operating bank: receives payment files, returns statements.
functions: Receives ACH and control-totals files over SFTP
Receives Positive Pay files for printed checks
Returns BAI2 statements daily
Validates test files in 48–72 hours; about 5 days to move a format to production

p2p.title: Procure to Pay: eight stages
p2p.lede: Suppliers are registered and qualified, requisitions and invoices are approved by amount tier, and payments leave as bank files. Accounting starts with the period-end accrual; invoice and payment follow through Subledger Accounting.

stages.title: Supplier onboarding
points: Supplier registration with approval for prospective and internal suppliers
Qualification questionnaires score business classifications (diversity)
DataFox enriches supplier records; an OIC interface updates classifications through REST
Go-live converted all suppliers with 18 months of AP history and 1099 flags

stages.title: Requisition
points: Approval by amount tier: to 5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, and over 250K
Supervisory hierarchy with named exceptions
P-card on requisitions is limited: the PO is created closed for receiving and card details don't reach AP

stages.title: Purchase order & contracts
points: Purchase orders, blanket and contract purchase agreements
Agreement change orders can auto-approve
Supplier contracts (MSA, CSA, SOW, NDA) stored with signed PDFs
Home-page tile shows contracts expiring this week

stages.title: Receipt
points: Receipts against POs complete the three-way match
No accounting at receipt: uninvoiced receipts accrue at period end
Only received-over-invoiced amounts accrue
POs leave the accrual report only when finally closed

entries.event: Period end: receipts not yet invoiced

stages.title: Invoice
points: Invoices arrive by email, are read by OCR and imported to Payables
Approval by amount tier; over 250K to an approval group
PO-matched and recurring invoices auto-approve
Imaging audit (imported not validated, deleted, not imported) tracked in ADW and OAC

stages.title: Payment
points: Payment process requests with approval by approval group
ACH file built in Oracle and sent straight to the bank's SFTP
Printed checks with a Positive Pay file
Corporate card spend reaches Payables through Expenses

cr: Cash, or Cash clearing (option not documented)

stages.title: Settlement
points: Bank A receives ACH, control-totals and Positive Pay files
BAI2 statements return daily and are reconciled in Cash Management
New file formats: transmission test, content validation in 48–72 hours, about 5 days to production

stages.title: Monitoring
points: Invoices processed and paid on time; % of invoices with a PO
Payment method mix: check, ACH, manual
Requisitions and POs by source (requisition, agreement, contract); new contracts and suppliers
Payables-to-ledger reconciliation in OTBI

p2p.accounting_note: Account types follow the Oracle Payables 26C defaults. Expense items accrue at period end and reverse when the next period opens. Whether payments are accounted at clearing (cash clearing) is not documented.

notes.title: Approvals are amount tiers.
notes.text: Requisitions and invoices share the same tiers (5K, 50K, 100K, 250K); the top tier goes to an approval group.

r2r.title: Record to Report: eight stages
r2r.lede: Daily policy journals, payroll and subledger accounting land in the ledgers of the Mutual and the Agency; intercompany and allocations run monthly; the close is driven from the EPM close task manager and ends on business day 6.

stages.title: Journals in
points: Daily policy journals (Premium, Loss, Claims) from the insurance data mart via a Financial Integrator
Premium and commission one day in arrears; case reserves two days
Payroll journal from ADP, mapped to Oracle accounts
A back-load chain reruns a missed load date

stages.title: Intercompany
points: Monthly shared-services billing from the Mutual to the Agency
The receiving organisation approves; batches transfer to GL
Settlement clears the receivable and payable against cash

stages.title: Allocations
points: Rule sets define source, target, range, basis and offset
A fixed point of view holds the segments that don't move
Results post to the allocation companies 81–89

stages.title: Fixed assets
points: Additions from Payables
Depreciation by book
Closed on business day 3–4

stages.title: Period-end adjustments
points: Uninvoiced receipts accrued at period end
Journals in accrual and adjustment categories auto-reverse on the first day of the next period
Journal approval by approval group

stages.title: Ledger close
points: Business day 6; may reopen for late statutory entries
Statutory balance sheet shows surplus, not retained earnings; Mutual and Agency differ
Year end: opening the new year rolls revenue and expense into retained earnings per balancing segment, without a journal
New segment values and hierarchies are published to the GL balances cube

stages.title: Close management & reconciliation
points: Close task manager holds the calendar, owners and sign-off
Account Reconciliation for balance sheet accounts (since September 2021)
Payables and Receivables to Ledger reconciliation in OTBI

stages.title: Reporting & planning
points: About 20 FRS statements: statutory balance sheet, statement of surplus, P&L by product and state, cash flow
Foundation not-for-profit statements and Agency statements
Narrative Reporting packages with review and sign-off
Planning budgets and statistical journals return to GL budget balances

r2r.accounting_note: Intercompany entries come from the source notebook. Allocation, revaluation-free accrual and fixed-asset types follow the Oracle 26C guides and Oracle standard. Premium and loss entries are typical insurance accounting shown for illustration; the source does not document them.

notes.title: Statutory view.
notes.text: Statutory statements show surplus rather than retained earnings; the Statement of Surplus is an FRS report.

fnd.title: Foundation & controls
fnd.lede: The structures and rules every transaction passes through: the chart of accounts, hierarchies, security, accounting rules and approval workflows.

stages.title: Enterprise structure
points: Mutual (company 10) and Agency (company 20) ledgers in one data set
Foundation (company 90) reports as a not-for-profit
Statutory company 80 and allocation companies 81–89
New subsidiary: company value, hierarchy, legal entity, balancing segment, ledger and BU assignments

stages.title: Chart of accounts
points: Company, Department, Account, Product, State, Class, Project, Intercompany
Product (line of business) and State support statutory reporting
Accounting Scenario values hold actual and budget versions

stages.title: Hierarchies & cube
points: Account and segment trees audited, flattened and published to the balances cube
New values reach the cube through the cube-update process
Bulk changes through the segment values and hierarchies import
Alternate hierarchies for sales channel and statistical accounts

stages.title: Security & validation
points: Segment value security on cost center and account
Data access sets per ledger and business-unit access for subledgers
Cross-validation rules and combination sets
Custom roles trimmed from seeded job roles

stages.title: Accounting rules & mappings
points: Subledger Accounting rule sets, account rules and mapping sets
Financial Integrator maps policy activity to GL accounts
ADP pay codes map to GL accounts
EPM Data Management maps GL to Planning and close

stages.title: Approval workflows
points: Requisitions and invoices by amount tier (5K, 50K, 100K, 250K, over 250K)
Payments, journals and invoices over 250K by approval group
Supplier registration and spend-authorisation approvals
Workflow Rules Report documents the configured rules

stages.title: Journal controls
points: Auto-reverse by category to the first day of the next period
Journal approval by approval group
Close by module from business day 1 to 6

stages.title: Change & release
points: Oracle updates each quarter (March, June, September, December)
Regression list: integrations, OTBI subject areas, Essbase, OneCloud chains
Post-refresh steps after copying production to test

notes.title: Why this matters.
notes.text: Most reporting and integration issues trace back to a mapping, a hierarchy not yet published to the cube, or a validation rule.

onboarding.title: Data & reporting
onboarding.lede: ADW is the finance data warehouse; Enterprise EPM handles planning and close; OAC and the Fusion reporting tools serve users. Each lane is a path data takes from Oracle to a report.

steps.label: BI Publisher report
steps.text: Data model and report in Fusion define the extract

steps.label: OIC scheduled orchestration
steps.text: Invokes the report web service, stages the file, inserts rows into an ADW table

steps.label: Bulk extract
steps.text: ESS extract job → business event → download to object storage or FTP

steps.label: ADW
steps.text: Finance report mart; spot checks compare report output with the table

lanes.title: Policy data to the ledger
lanes.route: Exceed → BIM (SQL Server) → ADW insurance data mart → Financial Integrator → GL

steps.label: Exceed
steps.text: Premium, commission, claims and case reserves

steps.label: BIM (SQL Server, on-premise)
steps.text: Policy, premium and claims reporting data; a load server copies it to ADW

steps.label: Insurance data mart (ADW)
steps.text: Stage and temp tables by load date

steps.label: Financial Integrator
steps.text: Maps activity to GL accounts; journal categories Premium, Loss, Claims

steps.label: General Ledger
steps.text: Daily journals; SQL checks tie back to source

lanes.title: EPM and cubes
lanes.route: GL → Data Management → Planning → OneCloud → OAC Essbase

steps.label: Data Management
steps.text: GL actuals to Planning; budgets back to GL

steps.label: OneCloud
steps.text: Loads Planning financials and ADW metrics into the OAC Essbase cube; backups

steps.label: OAC
steps.text: Dashboards and Smart View on the Essbase cube

lanes.title: Reporting layer
lanes.route: OTBI · BI Publisher · FRS · Smart View · OAC

steps.label: OTBI
steps.text: Real-time subject areas; reconciliation subject areas

steps.label: BI Publisher
steps.text: Custom reports to a content-cloud folder for Accounting

steps.label: FRS & Smart View
steps.text: Financial statements and ad hoc analysis on the GL balances cube

notes.title: Four types of finance reporting.
notes.text: Operational (OTBI, BIP), management (EPM, Essbase), enterprise analytics (OAC on ADW), regulatory (statutory statements).

notes.title: Reconciliation points.
notes.text: Account Reconciliation; Payables/Receivables to Ledger in OTBI; policy-feed SQL checks by load date; before/after extract checks.

notes.title: ADW as the warehouse.
notes.text: ADW is an Oracle Autonomous Database (Data Warehouse workload) holding transaction-level finance data. Fusion data reaches it through OIC and OneCloud, policy data through BIM; Data Sync was replaced by ODI / OCI Data Integration.

notes.title: Where Essbase sits.
notes.text: Two Essbase cubes: the OAC financials cube (from Planning via OneCloud) and the Fusion GL balances cube (FRS, Smart View, OTBI). EDW, BIM and HDS are SQL Server databases, and ADW is an Oracle Autonomous Database.

close.title: Close calendar
close.lede: Modules close in sequence from business day 1 to 6, managed in the EPM close task manager.

timeline.what: Policy journals (Premium, Loss, Claims) load one to two days in arrears
OneCloud and OIC loads into ADW and the OAC Essbase cube
Shared-services intercompany billing, Mutual to Agency
Uninvoiced receipt accruals created; reversed when the next period opens
General Ledger close; may reopen for late statutory entries
Account reconciliations; FRS statements; Narrative Reporting packages
Planning budgets and statistical journals to GL budget balances
Open the first period of the new year: revenue and expense roll to retained earnings

integrations.title: Integration register
integrations.lede: Interfaces documented in the source notebook, by name. State as of 2023; a working list, not a certified register.
